arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ryan McCortney argued that paying back wages to an undocumented worker conflicts with immigration laws.
He stated that the worker was never legally present or authorized to work in the country.
He cited violations of federal statutes regarding illegal entry and fraudulent employment documents.
The NLRB argued that undocumented workers are entitled to workers' compensation and tort damages in state courts.

The NLRB wants the back pay award to stand to protect the worker's labor rights.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the financial liability of employers who hire undocumented workers. It clarifies whether federal immigration law overrides labor protections for unauthorized employees. The outcome shapes workplace enforcement and compensation standards nationwide.
